audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Jax six of seven stages while every one of its whys except the last says the opposite — 'Jax is even at Level 1 and so are you', 'still even', 'out-trading his early all-in', 'stabilize the lane', 'punishes any greedy all-in', 'make you sticky and tanky'. It also sat on 7.5/10 difficulty against a 55.52% Cho'Gath win rate over 580 games.
audit.why: Levels 1-2 are even on one ability each. From 3, Rupture into Feral Scream beats his Q-W burst outright, and 6 through first item are Cho'Gath's. Only the two-item Trinity Force window is Jax's, and it is decisively his.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Skill / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Jax; difficulty re-rated 5/10 to match the FAV tag already on the entry.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phase whys were generic template text with no cooldowns; the level-6 line said only 'Jax's ultimate changes the math too'.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9s — a 17-second rank-1 cooldown is an enormous window and the page never gave the number while telling the reader to 'engage on Counter Strike's cooldown'. Leap Strike is 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s, Empower 7/6/5/4/3s, Grandmaster-at-Arms 110/100/90s and Feast 80/70/60s. Feast matters at 6 specifically because Grandmaster-at-Arms grants bonus armour and MR that true damage ignores.
audit.corrected: Counter Strike 17s, Leap Strike 8s, Grandmaster-at-Arms 110s and Feast 80s now appear in the phase, cooldown and interaction fields.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry told the reader 'don't throw a raw Rupture while his E is raised — he'll dodge your follow-up'. Riot's text says Counter Strike dodges all incoming attacks; it says nothing about abilities. Rupture and Feral Scream are not attacks and are not dodged.
audit.why: This inverts the correct play. What Counter Strike genuinely turns off is your basic attacks and therefore the Vorpal Spikes procs that ride them, so the rule is stop attacking, not stop casting. Rupture (950 range, flat 6s) still lands the knockup through a raised E, and Feral Scream (11s at rank 1) still silences — which is what denies the Counter Strike and Leap Strike casts in the first place. The missing-interactions file also notes his combo opens on an Empower auto-reset, so the wind-up is the tell.
audit.corrected: Counter Strike dodges attacks, not abilities — Rupture and Feral Scream still land on him.

edits.before: Jax is even-ish with you at Level 1, but the moment you have both Q and W you own the trade: bait out his E Counter Strike, then land Rupture for the knockup and immediately Feral Scream to silence him so he can't Counter Strike-stun or Q-leap out. Don't throw a raw Rupture while his E is raised — he'll dodge your follow-up and stun you mid-combo. Last-hit and chunk him with Vorpal Spikes, top up off Carnivore kills, and punish every time his Counter Strike is on cooldown.
edits.after: Jax is even-ish at Level 1, but once you have Q and W you own the trade: bait his E, then Rupture for the knockup and immediately Feral Scream so he can't Counter Strike-stun or Q-leap out. Counter Strike dodges attacks, not abilities — Rupture and Feral Scream still land through it, but your autos and Vorpal Spikes procs do not, so stop attacking while it is raised. Last-hit with Vorpal Spikes, top up off Carnivore, and punish every time his 17-second E is down.

notes: The biggest correction here is a reversed instruction: the entry told the reader not to cast Rupture into a raised Counter Strike because 'he'll dodge your follow-up'. Riot's text says Counter Strike dodges incoming attacks, and Rupture and Feral Scream are not attacks — the thing it actually shuts off is your basic attacks and the Vorpal Spikes procs riding them. I did not claim that silencing Jax cancels an already-active Counter Strike; Riot's text does not say, so the advice is to silence before he raises it. Packet flagged 'Pop Counter Strike' and 'Counter Strike-stun' as probable wrong names — both false positives. Cho'Gath's kit flags Rupture as 'grounding'; Riot's description says it pops enemies into the air, so I wrote knockup.
